D018-D011_h001.question:
It started after the car accident about eight months ago. Since then, it doesn’t feel like it ever really ended. I still see the truck coming at us when I close my eyes, and at least a few nights a week I jerk awake from these awful dreams where I’m back on that highway. I wake up sweating, heart racing, and it takes me a minute to remember I’m in my own bed.

I used to love reading and doing yoga after my shifts at the pharmacy, but now I just…don’t care. My husband keeps suggesting we go hiking like we used to, and I have zero interest. Mostly I just sit on the couch scrolling, feeling stuck on that moment of impact. The terror of it is still right there, like it just happened yesterday. I keep running through it and blaming the other driver, my husband for insisting we take that route, even myself for not insisting we stop earlier.

Day to day, I’m jumpy and on edge. If someone taps me on the shoulder at work, I practically jump out of my skin. Even simple decisions—what to wear, what to cook—can paralyze me. And the constant anxiety I feel is always tied back to being on the road, crashes, or something bad suddenly happening again.
D018-D011_h001.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D018-D011_h002.question:
It’s been a little over a year since the car accident, but it still feels like it’s happening. Sometimes when I’m driving, or even just hearing tires screech outside, it’s like I’m back there—my hands clamp on the wheel and for a few seconds I’m not in the present at all. I see the crash, hear the metal, and I honestly feel like it’s happening again.

Since then I’ve felt kind of numb. Things that used to make me happy—working on side projects, gaming with friends, even spending time with my kids—don’t really do anything for me. I go through the motions, but there’s no real enjoyment. I keep replaying that night and thinking it was my fault, that I should’ve reacted faster, taken a different route. I feel ashamed, like I failed everyone.

I’m on edge all the time. If someone walks into my office unexpectedly or a coworker moves quickly behind me, I jump out of my skin. My anxiety spikes, especially around driving routes near the crash site, so I avoid that area completely. Lately I’m forgetting small things—where I put my keys, what I was about to say in a meeting—because my mind is constantly stuck on that accident.
D018-D011_h002.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D018-D011_h003.question:

Ever since then, anything that even reminds me of that day just sets me off. If I hear screeching tires or see dash‑cam footage at work, it’s like I’m back there for a second—my chest tightens, my mind locks onto that moment, and I feel this surge of panic that can last for hours.

I can’t shake the image of his face or the sound of the impact. The terror from that instant just sits with me; it doesn’t fade. I find myself replaying it and getting angry, telling myself it was the track supervisor’s fault, or the company’s, even when I know it’s more complicated than that.

Since then I’ve been dragging myself through the day. I used to love digging into design problems; now I just stare at my CAD screen, foggy, like my brain’s moving through mud. When something suddenly startles me—like a loud bang in the shop—my heart races and my hands shake for a long time afterward. I avoid going near the test track, avoid driving at night. The constant anxiety and irritability all feel tied to that accident.
D018-D011_h003.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D018-D011_h004.question:

I’m angry all the time—at work, at home. Little things make me snap. Underneath that I keep thinking it was my fault, like if I’d yelled sooner or checked the machine better he’d still be alive.

I used to be pretty straightforward about decisions, but now even choosing what to eat or what clothes to wear before my shift can take forever. My mind gets stuck, worrying about all the “what ifs.” The anxiety is always there, but it feels tied to that night in the factory; everything circles back to it.

    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D018-D011_h005.question:

D018-D011_h006.question:

Even when I’m alone, if a thought about that night pops up, I feel this wave of panic and I’ll do anything to push it away—busywork, checking emails, anything just not to think about it.

There are pieces of that night I can’t seem to remember clearly, like parts of what he said or how I got behind the counter. But I remember his gun, his eyes. Most of the time now I just feel…blank. It’s like I’m on autopilot; things I used to enjoy at work mean nothing.

I’ve become really snappy with staff and guests. I’ll explode over minor mistakes, yelling or swearing, then feel awful later. I also feel constantly on edge and anxious at work, but it’s always tied back to that night—I’m always scanning the lobby, waiting for it to happen again.
D018-D011_h006.options:

    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h007.question:

For a few seconds I’m back in that stairwell—heart hammering, hands shaking, I can feel it happening again. It takes me a long time to come down from that; even after I realize I’m safe, my body doesn’t believe it.

I go out of my way to avoid anything that reminds me of that night—certain streets, after-hours fittings, even talking about it. I’ve also become really snappy; if someone questions a design or is late with payment, I’ll just explode—yelling, swearing, way out of proportion. I’m anxious all the time, but it’s always tied back, somehow, to that night. Even when I finish a collection or a big dress turns out beautifully, I just feel… nothing. No pride, no satisfaction, just emptiness and tension.
D018-D011_h007.options:

    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder

D018-D011_h008.question:

D018-D011_h009.question:

D018-D011_h012.question:

It really started after the accident three years ago, when that truck hit our car. Since then, it feels like a part of me is still stuck there. I still get this wave of sheer terror when I hear screeching brakes or see a truck in my rearview mirror—my heart pounds, my hands shake, I feel like I can’t breathe, like it’s happening all over again.

I’m anxious most days—on edge, jumpy, always scanning for danger—but it all circles back to that crash. I avoid riding in cars unless I absolutely have to, and I won’t go near that intersection. My kids want to take me on trips, but I make excuses because just thinking about the highway makes me panic.

I used to be very affectionate with my children and grandkids, but now I feel…blocked. I care about them, but it’s like I’m behind glass; I can’t feel warmth the same way, can’t say “I love you” without feeling hollow.
